overview: The input packet, also called steer vehicle, is sent every tick while riding a boat or horse, carrying forward and sideways axes plus the jump and unmount flags. It is the only stream that tells the server what the rider wants to do, so vehicle movement checks pair it with the vehicle move packet: impossible axis values, steering while not in a vehicle, and input that does not match the predicted vehicle motion are all C0C signatures. Boat fly and boat speed cheats are detected by comparing the claimed input against the vehicle's actual motion.

checks.name: VehicleA (Grim)
checks.purpose: Cancels steer vehicle packets whose forward or sideways axes exceed the physically possible range.
checks.how_it_works: PreViaPacketReceiveListener on STEER_VEHICLE: decodes WrapperPlayClientSteerVehicle and, if the absolute forward or sideways value is above 0.98, flags with both values in the verbose, cancels the packet and runs onPacketCancel. The 0.98 bound matches the vanilla input clamp.
checks.detects: Modified clients that send boosted input axes to move vehicles faster, and input spoofing modules.
checks.variations: VehicleB (same anticheat) cancels steer packets sent while the player is not in a vehicle; NCP routes the packet into its vehicle checks through InputsAdapter.

checks.name: InputsAdapter (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Feeds the steer vehicle packet into NCP's vehicle movement checks as an input queue.
checks.how_it_works: BaseAdapter listening at MONITOR priority on STEER_VEHICLE. It skips temporary players, resolves the IPlayerData and NetData, and wraps the raw Input object with an AutoWrapper into DataPacketInput, then pushes it onto the input queue. NCP's vehicle checks consume the queue to validate the rider's claimed input against the vehicle move. The javadoc notes the packet is named Player_Input in the modern protocol but ProtocolLib keeps the legacy name.
checks.detects: Feeds the input data used by VehicleChecks, VehicleEnvelope and VehicleMorePackets to flag boat fly and vehicle speed cheats.
checks.variations: Grim reads the steer packet directly in VehicleA and VehicleB; Intave SteerVehicleReader exposes the jump flag; BetterAnticheat RepeatedSteerCheck uses the packet rhythm instead.

checks.name: BoatFlyCheck (CheaterDeleter)
checks.purpose: Flags boats that rise without the rider providing the motion, the boat fly signature.
checks.how_it_works: VehicleMoveListener combining the player input packet with consecutive vehicle move packets. If the vehicle has no step height, the y delta is positive, and the vehicle's own velocity is not positive, it flags Boat Fly with the delta and velocity, then punishes by grounding the boat. Piston pushes and liquid contact within the last second are exempt.
checks.detects: Boat fly cheats that lift the boat without server-side motion to explain it.
checks.variations: Grim VehicleC and VehiclePredictionRunner compare the steer input against predicted vehicle motion; NCP VehicleEnvelope runs the same idea with an envelope model; Rammelkast AntiCheatReloaded BoatFlyCheck and MC-Jinky BoatCheck are the same pattern on older bases.

checks.name: RepeatedSteerCheck (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Flags artificial vehicle move streams that omit the rotation packet a real client sends between vehicle moves.
checks.how_it_works: Tracks a lastRotating flag: any flying packet with a rotation change sets it true; a VEHICLE_MOVE packet consumes it and sets it false. A vehicle move with lastRotating false fails the check, because the vanilla client always interleaves a rotation packet between vehicle move packets.
checks.detects: Vehicle move spoofers and boat fly modules that generate only vehicle move packets.
checks.variations: CheaterDeleter BoatFlyCheck inspects y motion, Grim VehicleA checks the input axes, and NCP validates the full move envelope.

checks.name: SteerVehicleReader (Intave)
checks.purpose: Reads the jump flag from the steer vehicle packet so the movement simulator knows when the rider wants to jump.
checks.how_it_works: AbstractPacketReader that reads the first boolean of the steer vehicle packet as isJumping. It is consumed by the vehicle simulation branch, the boat simulator and the keypress brancher, to predict the vehicle's motion from the rider's input.
checks.detects: Feeds the input state used by Intave's boat and vehicle physics simulation to catch vehicle fly and speed cheats.
checks.variations: Grim VehicleA and VehicleB validate the raw axes and vehicle state; NCP InputsAdapter queues the full input object; BetterAnticheat RepeatedSteerCheck checks packet rhythm.
